thread.title: Ninth Circuit clears path for foster youth civil rights case to move forward

author: First State Times
title: Ninth Circuit clears path for foster youth civil rights case to move forward
text:
The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit has ruled on May 20 that seven young people in Los Angeles County’s foster care system can proceed with a civil rights lawsuit against county and state agencies. The case, Ocean S. v. Los Angeles County, alleges that these agencies failed to provide safe housing, behavioral health services, and basic support to transition age foster youth—those between ages 16 and 21.
This decision is significant because it allows the plaintiffs to pursue systemic reforms they have sought since filing suit. Advocates say many young people in L.A. County’s foster care system face homelessness or unstable living situations and struggle to access mental health care due to longstanding gaps between legal requirements and actual services provided.
According to Public Counsel, attorneys and social workers have seen firsthand the trauma experienced by transition age foster youth who are separated from their families and do not receive promised support once they turn 18. The complaint describes cases where young people with mental health disabilities ended up homeless, hospitalized, or assaulted as a result of these failures in care.
Public Counsel said: “Our clients brought this case to ensure that young people in foster care receive the basic housing, services, and support the law promises them.” The organization added it is honored to stand with these individuals alongside co-counsel Alliance for Children’s Rights, Children’s Rights, and pro bono partner Munger, Tolles & Olson LLP.
The ruling means that urgent issues raised by transition age foster youth will now be addressed in court rather than dismissed at an early stage. Public Counsel said it will continue seeking accountability and lasting change within L.A. County’s foster care system.
